messages.subject: Re: ldply rename variables
messages.body_plain:
The documentation says

     "The most unambiguous behaviour is achieved when ‘.fun’ returns a
     data frame - in that case pieces will be combined with
     ‘rbind.fill’.  If ‘.fun’ returns an atomic vector of fixed length,
     it will be ‘rbind’ed together and converted to a data frame. Any
     other values will result in an error."

So in my view the better way is

ldply(mtcars, function(x) data.frame(mean=mean(x)))

Best,
Ista

amount.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Mon, Feb 18, 2013 at 3:48 PM, Ross Ahmed <ross...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> Is there an equivalent to sapply using plyr?

Depends on what you mean by this I suppose.

>
> Example:
>
> dat <- rnorm(1000)
> sapply(seq(10, 100, 10), function(x) mean(sample(dat, x)))
>
> The closest I can get using plyr is:
>
> unlist(llply(seq(10, 100, 10), function(x) mean(sample(dat, x))))
>
> Is there a plyr function, without having to use unlist?

ply functions are named according to the expected input and desired
output. For example, ddply takes a data.frame and returns a
data.frame. ldply takes a list and returns a list. So if you do not
want a list don't use llply, but rather laply:

set.seed(10)
x1 <- sapply(seq(10, 100, 10), function(x) mean(sample(dat, x)))

library(plyr)
set.seed(10)
x2 <- laply(seq(10, 100, 10), function(x) mean(sample(dat, x)))

all.equal(x1, x2)

Best,
Ista

messages.subject: Has summarize in plyr changed?
messages.body_plain:
I often use ddply in combination with summarize to, well, summarize variables. Sometimes the summary of one variable is contingent on the value of another variable:

library(plyr)
df <- data.frame(G=rep(1:2,each=50), ACC=sample(0:1, 100, replace=TRUE), RT=rnorm(100,400,20))
df.m <- ddply(df, .(G), summarise, ACC=mean(ACC), RT=mean(RT[ACC==1]))

This used to work fine, but as of the latest update (R 2.15.2 & plyr 1.8) it is now broken. It appears that the reference to ACC in the definition of the RT summary variable is now picking up the summary variable ACC instead of the variable ACC in the subset of the data frame.

This seems like a fundamental change in how summarize works that will silently alter the output of a lot of existing code. Is this change intentional? If so, is there a way to use the old functionality of summarize, or to make it explicit when I want to refer to a column in the data frame and not a new summary variable?

Thanks,
Adam

messages.subject: Re: Has summarize in plyr changed?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Yes, this improvement (and it really is an improvement!) was added
last Summer (see https://github.com/hadley/plyr/pull/89). summarize
works sequentially, so you just need to change the order:

df.m <- ddply(df, .(G), summarise, RT=mean(RT[ACC==1]), ACC=mean(ACC))

Best,
Ista
